exposure: mode of delivery (Caesarean-section vs vaginal deliveries)
cohort: The study included 24,392 twin-pairs from Ontario, Canada, born between 2004-2017, and followed them until they were 1 to 15 years old.
finding: Male-female and male-male twin-pairs had higher odds of asthma discordance compared to female-female pairs, and twins delivered by Caesarean-section had significantly higher odds of asthma and allergic rhinitis discordance, with strong suggestions for eczema discordance.
mod_finding: Twins delivered by Caesarean-section, compared to vaginal deliveries, had significantly higher odds of asthma (aOR:1.09) and allergic rhinitis (aOR:1.11), with associations also suggested for eczema discordance (aOR:1.05).
